accuracy.evidence: Every number was recomputed: 342 + 10 = 352, 342 - 10 = 332, 342 +/- 100 = 442/242, 875 - 4 x 100 = 475, 386 + 20 = 406, 395 + 10 = 405, 503 - 10 = 493, 900 + 100 = 1000, 598 + 10 = 608, 129 + 1 = 130; the 507 cross (407, 497, 517, 607) and all six sort cards were checked by script. The curriculum wording matches NC England Year 3 Number and place value ('find 10 or 100 more or less than a given number') and CCSS 2.NBT.8. Parameter ranges keep every answer inside 100-999 except the stated 1000 case.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips for this objective: changing the ones digit (343), changing the wrong place (442 for 10 more, 630 for 100 less), going the wrong way for 'less', missing the exchange across a hundred (3105, 305 for 395 + 10; 403 for 503 - 10) and reading the size of a change from the digit that moved (129 to 130, 598 to 608). The NCETM place-value materials name the exchange and the zero-tens case as the hard points.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is built on base-ten blocks in a hundreds/tens/ones chart: adding a ten rod moves only the tens digit, taking a hundred flat moves only the hundreds digit, and the 10th rod forces a 10-tens-for-1-hundred swap. The 507 cross and the 'changed by 1/10/100' sort are specific to 10 and 100 more or less; the gate measures it under 30% similar to every other flagship lab, and no other lab uses a regrouping chart driven by single +10/-100 moves.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner picks which block makes 10 more (a flat or cube gives feedback naming 100 more or 1 more and does not change the chart), watches the lit digit show that only one place changes, meets the full Tens column and has to swap it, then applies the rule without blocks in the cross and finally sees that crossing a boundary changes two digits even for a 1 or 10 change. The text after each task confirms what the blocks showed.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'The ones: 343' for 342 + 10 (only the tens digit lights up), '865' for 100 less than 875 (taking a flat gives 775), and '3106' for 396 + 10 (the 10 rods must be swapped, giving 406). The step's done message names what the learner predicted.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with answers in rotating positions; every wrong option carries a slip tag with its own message: 'ones' (that changes the ones digit, so 1 more or less), 'tens', 'hund' (changed the wrong place), 'cross' (a column holds at most 9; swap 10 tens for 1 hundred) and 'dir' (more makes it bigger, less makes it smaller). Wrong drops in the lab also name the slip, e.g. '407 is 100 less ... 507 has 0 tens, so take 1 hundred as 10 tens: 497'.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the readability limits (kid at most 6.5, adult at most 9.5). Kid paragraphs use short sentences with concrete words (ten, hundred, digit, place) and one worked number each. Canvas prompts are one line ('Make 10 more each time, from 342 to 382'), digits are 32-40 px, column labels 14-16 px.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one rule: what each digit counts and 10 more or less; 100 more or less; regrouping past 9; judging the size of a change. Adult paragraphs give the curriculum statements and key words, why the digits stay the same, the named mistakes, and what the lab does. The filler gate passes and no sentence repeats template text.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark and at desktop for every step before and after Show me. Fixes made from screenshots: the tray ten rod was drawn off-centre over its label after rotating (now centred with the value above it), and the '100 more' label sat on the connector line in the cross (now under the box, with tiles moved down). Columns are about 110 px wide and the full column height is a tap target; tiles and cards are at least 52 px tall.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin with a descriptive aria-label, including the wrong choices ('Put a hundred flat in the Hundreds column of 342', 'Take a ten rod away from 875', 'Swap 10 ten rods for 1 hundred flat', 'Put 497 in the 10 less gap', '129 to 130 goes in Changed by 1'); the canvas aria-label is updated live with each reply; the challenge uses real buttons and a polite live region; axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and phone in the browser gate.

sources: DfE (2013) National Curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study, Year 3 Number and place value ('find 10 or 100 more or less than a given number'; 'recognise the place value of each digit in a three-digit number')
Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, 2.NBT.8 ('Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100-900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100-900')
NCETM (2017) Mastery Professional Development materials: Number, Place value (exchanging 10 tens for 1 hundred; zero as a placeholder)
